intro_html: Smoked turkey sausage over cheesy parmesan grits with an egg on top, this is Southern breakfast-for-dinner that works any hour. Each bowl carries 25 grams of protein for about $3.28 (at everyday cost), and it is a genuinely cheap bowl.
cost_closing_html: About $3.28 a bowl (at everyday cost) for sausage, cheesy grits, and an egg. A brunch spot charges $12 for this plate plus a wait for a table. You have 14 servings and no line.
shop_smart: Smoked turkey sausage at about $8.86 for 2.75 pounds is pre-cooked, pre-seasoned protein. You are paying for flavor someone else already built, which is rare good value in the meat case.
Grits are one of the last truly cheap staples standing, the canister covers this batch and several more. Old-fashioned grits cost the same as quick and taste better.
Eggs pull double duty as protein and topping at roughly $0.10 to $0.20 each depending on the week. One egg per bowl is the cheapest protein add-on in the store.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Bring the chicken broth plus enough water for your grits ratio to a boil, then whisk in the grits slowly. Drop the heat to low and simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 20 minutes.
Stir the parmesan into the grits with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder.
While the grits cook, slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in the olive oil with the onion until both pick up color. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes for the last minute.
Cook the eggs: bring a pot of water with the white vinegar to a bare simmer and poach the eggs 3 to 4 minutes, or fry them if that is more your speed. For meal prep, slightly firm yolks hold up best.
Build bowls: cheesy grits down, sausage and onions over the top, egg on top of that.
Reheat gently with a splash of water stirred into the grits, they tighten up in the fridge and loosen right back.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot of grits and sausage, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14, then add one egg per container. Each bowl lands at about 561 calories with 25 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $3.28 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.keywords: turkey sausage and grits, cheesy grits recipe, southern meal prep, budget breakfast for dinner, grits bowl, cheap meal prep
steps: Simmer grits in broth and water until thick, then stir in parmesan and seasonings.
Brown sliced turkey sausage with onion and garlic in olive oil.
Poach the eggs in simmering water with vinegar, or fry them.
Build bowls with grits, sausage, and an egg each, then portion into 14 containers.
